# erp-core usage

You are building on erp-core 1.6.0. The manifest in `reference/core-manifest.yaml` is the only description of the core you may rely on; `reference/conventions.md` and `reference/modules/` are the same documents the core repository publishes for this version.

<!-- KEEP:body:START -->
## Workflow — search before you create

1. **Before creating any entity, service or endpoint**, open `reference/core-manifest.yaml` and search
   `modules.*.provides` and `modules.*.entities` / `tables` for the thing you are about to build (users, roles,
   lookups, files, documents, images, notifications, templates, number series, settings, audit, reports, exports,
   tenants). Search by meaning, not only by the exact word: a "customer account" is `sec` (`customer-accounts`),
   a "status list" is `mdl` (`lookups`), an "attachment" is `file`, a "counter" is `sequence`.
2. **If the core has it, use it** through the module's `extension-points` (a bean you implement) or `interfaces`
   (a bean you inject) exactly as `reference/modules/<module>.md` § How to call it shows; read that file before
   writing the call. Never duplicate the capability, never copy a core class, never read a core table except as
   the manifest's shared entities allow.
3. **If the core does not have it**, build it in the application's own package under its own module prefix,
   following every convention below; `templates/business-module/` is the shape of a correct module.
4. **If the core almost has it** (a missing field, a missing method, a missing event), it is a core gap — see the
   last section. Never a local copy, never a workaround.
5. Review the result against `templates/checklist.md` before calling the module done.

## Conventions — one checkable sentence each

- **Tenancy** — every table carries `TENANT_ID` with FK, index and composite uniques, every entity extends
  `AuditableEntity`, no code reads `erp.core.tenant.mode` or `default-tenant-id`, the tenant comes from
  `TenantContext`, jobs go through `TenantRunner` ([reference](reference/conventions.md#tenancy)).
- **Lookups** — every user-maintained code list is an MDL lookup type seeded by `V1000+` and read through
  `MdlLookupApi.readActiveValuesByKey`; the module stores the code and never an enum of codes
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#lookups)).
- **Files** — every byte goes through `FilePrivateStoreApi`, `FileImageStoreApi` or the FILE endpoints and is
  referenced by `FILE_DOCUMENT.ID`; no `java.io.File`, no S3 client in business code
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#files)).
- **Notifications** — every message is `NotificationDispatchApi.dispatch(DispatchCommand)` with a seeded
  `NOTIF_TEMPLATE` code; a new channel is a `ChannelProvider` bean ([reference](reference/conventions.md#notifications)).
- **Numbering** — every document number is `NumberSeriesApi.next(code)` from a `V1000+`-seeded series, stored in
  a column unique with `TENANT_ID` ([reference](reference/conventions.md#numbering)).
- **Reporting** — every list export or tabular report is one `ReportProvider` bean and every printed document goes
  through `PrintApi`; the module has no `/export` endpoint of its own ([reference](reference/conventions.md#reporting)).
- **Error codes** — every error is `LocalizedException(Status, <Module>ErrorCodes.X, args)` with an EN and an AR
  message in the application's bundles; no raw runtime exception reaches the client
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#error-codes)).
- **Auth and permissions** — the module declares one `PermissionContributor` (`<Module>Permissions`, a `VIEW` per
  screen) and guards every service method with `@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority(T(…<Module>Permissions).PERM_…)")`
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#auth-and-permissions)).
- **Settings** — every operator-changeable value is read through `SettingsApi` (`getOrDefault`, `find`, `get`) under
  a `<MODULE>_<NAME>` key; no module config table, no `@Value` on `erp.core.*`
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#settings)).
- **Migrations** — the application owns `V1000+` only, `V<N>__<module>_<snake_case>.sql`, sequential, additive
  once shipped, every table with the foundation columns and `SEQ_<TABLE>`
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#migrations)).
- **Modules** — the module ships `META-INF/erp/modules/<code>.yaml` (`templates/business-module/module-manifest.yaml`)
  naming its `package`, `depends`, `permission-modules` and `api-paths`; it never checks its own licence (the core
  hides and refuses an unentitled module); a business event another module consumes goes through
  `OutboxPublisher` / `OutboxSubscriber`; it uses another business module's classes only when that module is in
  `depends` (`ModuleBoundaryRules`, one CI job per module — `templates/ci/module-matrix.yml`); a key figure on the
  home screen is a `home-cards` entry of the manifest valued by the module's one `HomeCardProvider` bean (read-only;
  the core gates, times and orders it — `templates/business-module/i18n/` holds the title keys)
  ([reference](reference/conventions.md#modules)).
- **Ledger** — a module that handles money maps its account roles to `GlAccountLookupApi` `accountId`s (never codes),
  posts each document once through `GlPostingApi.post` with a stable `idempotencyKey` of its own (a repeat answers
  `alreadyPosted = true`; a change is a new entry under a new key), reads totals back through `GlEntryQueryApi` and
  stores no journal, balance or chart of its own ([reference](reference/conventions.md#ledger)).

## Forbidden — a reviewer rejects the module on sight

- Reading `erp.core.tenant.mode` or `erp.core.tenant.default-tenant-id` anywhere in the module (`TenancyModeIsolationRules`
  fails the build).
- A native query or `JdbcTemplate` statement that bypasses the tenant filter: no `TENANT_ID` predicate, or no
  `@TenantUnscoped(reason, adr)` on its repository method.
- A hardcoded lookup code list: an enum, a `Map`, a `switch` over codes a user may maintain, or a table of codes
  outside MDL.
- Direct file-system or S3 access for business content (`java.io.File`, `java.nio.file.Files`, `S3Client`, a
  multipart endpoint of the module).
- A second authentication, permission or settings mechanism: a user / role / permission / grant / session table, a
  login or JWT filter, a filter chain, a settings or parameters table, `@Value` on an `erp.core.*` key.
- A module counter for document numbers: a counter table or column, `MAX(no) + 1`, a database sequence read for a
  number a user sees.
- A second export path: a CSV / XLSX / PDF writer, an `/export` endpoint, a report permission of your own.
- Error handling of your own: a raw `RuntimeException` / `IllegalArgumentException` reaching the client, a hard-coded
  message string, an error code without both its AR and EN bundle entries, a second `@ControllerAdvice` for the
  shared codes.
- Sending of your own: a `JavaMailSender`, an SMTP or SMS client in business code, a template or message table of
  your own, a retry loop around a send.
- Any copy of a core class, any `com.erp.*` package in the application, any edit to a core migration (`V1..V999`).
- A licence or subscription check of your own: a module on/off setting, a menu filter, an `if (licensed)` around an
  operation, a branch on the deployment mode — and a business event between modules sent through the in-process
  `DomainEventPublisher` (it cannot be replayed) or a per-module event table.

## Reporting a core gap

When the core almost has what you need — a missing field on a shared entity, a missing method on an interface, a
missing event, a missing convention — write an ADR **in the consuming project** named `CORE-GAP-<topic>.md`
(for example `CORE-GAP-file-category-per-owner.md`) in that project's ADR location, with: the capability searched
(the `provides` tokens and the module), what exists today (the interface or entity and why it is not enough), the
smallest additive change to erp-core that closes the gap (a new method with a default, a nullable column, a new
event — the MINOR rules of the core's `RELEASE.md`), and the module work that waits on it. Then build the module
**without** the capability or behind a clearly named `TODO(CORE-GAP-<topic>)` seam — never a workaround that
reimplements the core's part in the module, because that workaround is exactly what the next core version will
make a duplicate. The gap is raised to the erp-core repository as a pull request or a prompt; the module moves to
the new core version when it ships.
